topology_reasoning.device: Symmetric directional coupler (2x2). Two single-mode waveguides enter from left and right at +/-1.74 um from the device centerline, S-bend inward to a long central coupling region where they run parallel with a sub-wavelength gap, then S-bend back apart. Mirror-symmetric about both axes.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: In the coupling region the evanescent fields of the two closely spaced waveguides overlap; power transfers periodically between them with beat length set by the even/odd supermode index difference. The coupling length and gap set the power splitting ratio; the S-bends adiabatically bring the guides together so coupling is dominated by the straight central section.
function_defining_knobs: coupling_gap_um - edge-to-edge gap in the central section; exponentially controls coupling strength
coupling_length_um - length of the parallel central section; sets transfer ratio together with the gap
wg_width_um - guide width; sets mode confinement and supermode splitting
port_pitch_um - vertical separation of the input/output ports (decoupled spacing)
sbend_length_um - horizontal extent of the S-bends; adiabaticity of the approach

knob_verification.why_tool_fails_structurally: The checker enforces an MZI two-arm contract: lengths.json delta_length_um = |L_arm1 - L_arm2| must move by delta_um. A symmetric directional coupler has two equal-length arms; no function knob (gap, coupling length, width) changes the arm-length DIFFERENCE, so check (a) cannot pass for this device class. Area check (b) likewise assumes a length-extending knob. lengths.json contract is honored (arms computed from the built gf.Path segments at build time).
knob_verification.direct_geometry_proof: Perturbed coupling_gap_um 0.18 -> 0.28 in a copied script, rebuilt, measured the actual edge-to-edge gap from GDS polygons (gdstk) in the coupling section: 0.1800 -> 0.2800 um, delta exactly 0.100. The knob moves real geometry. See knob_response.json (field direct_gap_check).
